title: Effectiveness Conclusion — Factory Evaluation

q1_didFactoryLiteOutperformVanilla.evidenceBasis: Scored rubric: RUN-B (94) vs RUN-A (86). Factory Lite added +8 points on 100-point scale. Key gains: better test coverage (30 vs 19, with recorded results), EJS UI with views covering all pages, better structured code (src/ separation), and Manual Router + Proof-of-Read maintained contamination integrity.
q1_didFactoryLiteOutperformVanilla.caveats: Both RUN-A and RUN-B use sql.js (same WASM-based DB). Quality delta may partly reflect the builder rather than the Factory mechanism. RUN-A is competent — the Factory Lite process produced modest but real improvements.

q2_didRoleAgentOutperformFactoryLite.evidenceBasis: Scored rubric: RUN-C (93) vs RUN-B (94). Role-Agent scored -1 point lower than Factory Lite despite 7.8x more process overhead. RUN-C's better architecture (React SPA, better-sqlite3, schema.sql) was offset by: NO README (-4 points vs RUN-B's perfect docs), tests never run (CANNOT VERIFY, -2 points vs RUN-B's 30/30 PASS).
q2_didRoleAgentOutperformFactoryLite.caveats: RUN-C's architecture is objectively better than RUN-B's (better-sqlite3 > sql.js, React SPA > EJS, dedicated schema.sql > inline DDL). If tests were run and README existed, RUN-C would likely score highest. This suggests Role-Agent overhead diverted effort from critical deliverables (README, running tests) to process artifacts (profiles, contracts, handoffs).

keep: Manual Router — Low overhead (~100ms), prevents scope leakage. Both RUN-B and RUN-C benefited.
Proof-of-Read — Ensures agent reads requirements before building. Both Factory runs used it.
Evidence hierarchy — Separating process evidence from product evidence prevents false confidence.
Contamination log — Critical for multi-run benchmarks. All runs maintained clean separation.
cut: Role-Specialized Agent Company Model (10 roles) — For an 11-FR project, 10 roles is excessive. The overhead of role handoffs, cross-role contracts, and por receipts consumed effort that should have gone to product quality (README, running tests). A 3-role model (Architect, Builder, Reviewer) would be more appropriate.
defer: Cross-role contracts — Useful for larger projects with actual separate agents, but for single-agent simulation they add process artifacts without quality benefit.
Drift detection — Conceptually valuable but current implementation adds logging without preventing drift.
Security/QA/Verifier/Auditor as separate review roles — For projects with dedicated QA engineers these are essential. For single-agent benchmarks, fold review into a single Reviewer role.
rework: Role handoffs — Handoff format should be lighter. Current 8-handoff structure for a single-agent build is process theater.
Process overhead tracking — Should distinguish between 'process that prevented errors' and 'process that documented itself'.

q4_excessiveMechanisms: 10-role company model for an 11-FR project — 5 implementation roles for a monolith is over-segmentation
8 cross-role contracts between roles that never ran independently
Verifier + Auditor as separate roles when their checks overlap significantly
Architecture decision records as JSON (useful but shouldn't substitute for README)

q5_didFactoryPreventSimplification.evidenceBasis: RUN-C included architecture docs and process artifacts that are valuable but the role structure consumed effort that prevented completing a README and running tests. The Factory process didn't prevent simplification — it incentivized process artifact creation over product completeness. A simpler Factory (like Factory Lite) achieved better product quality with less overhead.

q6_recommendationsForFactoryEval9.summary: FACTORY-EVAL-9 should create Factory v0.4 with: KEEP Manual Router + Proof-of-Read, CUT 10-role model to 3-role, REWORK handoff format to be lighter, DEFER cross-role contracts to multi-agent projects only.
cut: 10-role company model (replace with 3-role: Architect, Builder, Reviewer)
defer: Drift detection (needs prevention, not just logging)

overallConclusion: Factory Lite demonstrated real, measurable product quality improvement over Vanilla (+8 points on 100-point rubric) with modest overhead (+200ms). The Role-Agent model did NOT outperform Factory Lite (-1 point despite 7.8x overhead), primarily due to process overhead diverting effort from critical deliverables. The Factory concept is validated — but the Role-Agent company model as currently designed is excessive for single-agent builds of this scope.
